title: Police admit car speeding before Edmonton crash
article: Police acknowledged an unmarked police car carrying two on-duty officers was speeding when it crashed into a vehicle Saturday morning, leaving two children clinging to life in hospital.

Giovanni Aleman, 7, and his brother Jonathon, 6, are in critical condition and undergoing surgery for severe burns and other serious injuries as a result of the crash that sliced their grandfather's Ford Tempo in half, sending them flying onto Yellowhead Trail covered in flames.
Doctors don't know if they will survive.
"Clearly speed was involved here," Edmonton police Supt. Bill Mowbray said Monday.
"You don't get this kind of damage, these kinds of injuries, if excessive speed is not involved."
Long, black skid marks followed the police Crown Victoria through the intersection, where there is a 70 km/h speed zone.
Witnesses and an officer on scene said the police car roared through a yellow light, but Mowbray said he could not confirm that.
Mowbray said four expert collision investigators are trying to determine details of the accident, including witness accounts the police car did not have on lights or sirens.
Mowbray said the officers were on patrol duty and not responding to a call, but they could have seen or heard something to cause them to race off.
He said the investigation will also look into whether stress played a role in the crash.
The two tactical team officers witnessed the suicide of a fellow officer on May 14.
Two days later, they were involved in the shooting of a drunk man who lunged at them with a butcher knife. One of the two officers fired the shots that killed John Pavic.
The officers, on the force for about 10 years, took time off after the two traumatic events and returned to work about a week before the crash.
